name: Firstborn of Lot
overview: The Firstborn of Lot is a female figure noted in Scripture primarily for her role as the mother of Moab. While her tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, her significance is tied to her unique position in the Genesis narrative. She is identified through her relationship to Lot and her offspring, which connects her to the origins of the Moabite people.
namesAndTitles: This individual is referred to simply as the 'firstborn of Lot,' a descriptive title found in Genesis 19:31. No Hebrew or Greek meaning is provided for this designation, and it serves as a straightforward description rather than a personal name or title given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that she is the daughter of Lot and the mother of Moab. These relationships establish her place within the biblical genealogy and link her to significant historical lineages. Beyond these, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The Firstborn of Lot is significant because she is the progenitor of Moab, from whom the Moabite nation descends, as stated in Genesis 19:37. Her role underscores the origins of a people who later appear in the biblical narrative, often in relation to Israel. Her story highlights the complex family dynamics and covenantal history that frame the unfolding of God’s plan in Scripture.
